checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: The arena lists sl-5pct, hold-12h, control, entry-8pct, placebo, tp-7pct and vol-4x as [running/confirm], i.e. as arms in the confirm stage.
findings.problem: The confirm sample is planned at n=600 per arm, but live_n is 12, 13, 13, 3, 13, 13 and 7 respectively — under 3% of the planned sample for the best-populated arm. Labelling these 'confirm' invites reading their screen numbers as confirm evidence when no arm has accumulated a decidable live sample.

findings.claim: screen_dWR of +5.29pp for sl-5pct and +3.23pp for hold-12h are presented as the arms' headline deltas.
findings.problem: These are screen numbers on backfill-derived detections (events by tier: backfill 4764 vs live 49), while the checklist itself states only live-tape evidence can promote. Quoting screen_dWR next to a 'running/confirm' status blurs the tier boundary; the deltas carry no promotion weight and should not be read as progress toward the objective.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is reported on the same footing as the other arms with screen_n=496 and screen_dWR=0.0pp.
findings.problem: Its screen_n is roughly a third of control's 1550 and vol-4x's is 866, so these arms are not scored on the same event population as control despite the header asserting 'all arms share identical detections'. A filtering arm necessarily drops events, so any WR/EV comparison against control's 1550 is unpaired unless control is restricted to the same subset — and no such restriction is reported.

findings.claim: Checklist paired_population is green: '4813 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them'.
findings.problem: Seeing an event is not scoring an event. entry-8pct scored 496 and vol-4x 866 out of control's 1550, so the green check establishes shared detection, not shared scoring. As stated it reads as a paired-comparison guarantee that the per-arm screen_n values contradict.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is listed as running with live_n=3 and screen_ev=-0.055.
findings.problem: Three resolved live trades is not a running arm in any evidentiary sense, and its screen EV is the only negative one in the arena. It is occupying an entry_trigger slot alongside control, which also holds class=entry_trigger, so the enforced one-arm-per-mechanism-class diversity is not actually satisfied by the running set.

findings.claim: Ghost arrival is stated as 25.2 control trades/day under STATISTICAL REALITY.
findings.problem: The graveyard entry L-dedup-0h cites 25.6 control trades/day as the same baseline. The two figures disagree and no n or window is attached to either, so any projection of how long confirm n=600 takes rests on an unreconciled arrival rate.
